submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole fires on the token that finishes a memorized multi-token string rather than a freely chosen word: its peaks are the non-initial digit chunk of a numeral the tokenizer split (2023 -> ' 20'+'23', 1874 -> ' 18'+'74', 1429 -> ' 14'+'29', 1763 -> ' 17'+'63'), weaker on whole numeral tokens inside date/quantity phrases (' in 1916', ' 1920s', '30 years'), and its other strong peaks are the second element of lexicalized two-word chunks ('made up', 'made of', 'study of', 'World War', 'Great Depression', 'twelve-year-old', 'bluegrass', ' was born'). It sits at baseline on ordinary compositional prose and on the same surface strings in non-lexicalized frames ('the king of France' 0.04, 'a blue grass field' 0.09, 'a Great Recession' 0.10, 'a well known author' 0.07); a few rare-word and acronym fragments ('CB|MS', 'mur|de|rers', 'w|ande|rer') fire strongly but are token-specific leftovers that this rule does not cover.

Would you like to travel to Washington, D.C. for a fully funded professional development conference and learn about civics education?
Then you should apply today to attend one of C-SPAN’s 2019 Summer Educator Conferences.
What Are C-SPAN’s Summer Educator Conferences?
Each year, C-SPAN hosts two Summer Educator Conferences at their office in Washington, D.C.
Each conference lasts two days, and attendees will be exposed to the extensive free resources provided by C-SPAN for classroom teachers. You’ll meet the staff behind C-SPAN classroom along with some of the staff responsible for producing C-SPAN’s video content and video library.
Another highlight of the conference is the dinner on the first night of the conference. Conference attendees attend a fancy dinner at one of city’s hotels, and they are joined by a special guest who will speak on a topic related to civics and education. Past guests include Richard Baker, Senate Historian, and Steve Scully, one of C-SPAN’s political correspondents.
This is also a great way to explore C-SPAN’s offerings and prepare to apply for C-SPAN’s Teacher Fellowship – which is an even greater summer professional development opportunity.
You can read more about C-SPAN’s Summer Educator Conferences on their website here.
How Do I Apply to Attend a C-SPAN Summer Educator Conference?
There are two Educator Conferences – one for Middle School teachers on July 22 and 23, and one for High School Teachers on July 25 and 26.
Select the appropriate dates, and then complete the application here. You’ll have to provide a short narrative about what you hope to learn at the conference.
Completed applications are due Friday, April 5.
If you’re looking for a more extensive professional development opportunity with C-SPAN, you should consider applying for the month-long Teacher Fellowship. Read more about that here.

Energy Efficient Homes: Be a Part of the Solution
Making your home energy efficient can be achieved in a few easy steps.
Before we recommend ways to make your home energy efficient, let’s look at the kind of lighting that is and can be used.
Incandescent lights: These are your traditional 100W, 60W and 40W bulbs and are highly – in fact, the most – inefficient in terms of energy use. A mere 10% of the energy is actually converted to light, the rest is lost as heat.
Tubelights: They come in a range, T5, T8 and T12, signifying thickness and are indirectly proportional to efficiency, i.e., T12 is least efficient. A T5 (28W) would save you half the energy when compared to a T12 (55W). Sure, T5’s are comparatively expensive but enjoy a longer lifespan. Remember, over time, tubelights dim out.
CFLs: For many years now, CFLs have been considered the most energy efficient. The percentage of energy saved by using CFL over incandescent light is roughly 70%, with a longer lifespan too.
LEDs: Definitely the latest, and highly recommended, technology in the category of energy-efficient lighting options for your home. With LED, you save 50% more than CFL – that’s a sizeable chunk of your electricity bill too. LED remains unchallenged in giving you a long life of 10 to 25 years and come with solid replacement warrantees that last a decade. Once installed, they are free of maintenance, requiring little or no repairs. Though comparatively more expensive, this is a negligible one-time investment considering the paybacks.
Tips to make your home energy efficient:
- LED lighting: Convert to low voltage LED lighting.
- Wear the right clothes: Layer up in the cold and go for loose cotton clothing in the summer so you do not have to depend on external sources to regulate the temperature for you.
- Unplug: Switch off all lights and fans when not in use.
- Standby power: It is a colossal waste to leave your electronic appliances plugged when not in use. Research shows that standby power accounts for more than 10% of a home’s electricity usage.
- Solar energy: This is a sustainable, renewable source of energy. If not 100%, do away with geysers, using solar for your heating needs.
- Refrigerator: It is common for Indian households to have nothing more than curry leaves, curd and milk in the fridge. Be aware of your needs and purchase an aptly sized fridge, not for the sake of fashion, fad or status. Since your fridge remains on always, it ranks very high on energy consumption. Especially, stay away from ones with enormous freezers if you do not have use for them. Keep the fridge door tightly closed at all times If you are a household with two fridges or freezers, switch on the second one on a need-to basis.
- Energy saving consumer goods: These are commonly available. Do your research and make it a habit to consult labels to ensure you are buying an efficient product. Educate yourself about the Energy Star (https://www.energystar.gov/).

This short book gives the reader a concise and straightforward insight into the achievements of John Moffat and one of the Second World War’s most infamous sea battles, the Royal Navy’s frantic search and subsequent sinking of the Bismarck in May 1941.
John Moffat: Legend of the Bismarck is the second chapter of British Flying Legends a new book by Richard Edwards and this particular chapter is around the length of a short story, approximately 35 printed pages.
In addition to exploring John Moffat’s early life and his role in the sinking of the Bismarck, this book also looks at the dramatic sinking of HMS Hood and the loss of over 1,400 of her crew during the short Battle of the Denmark Strait, the story of HMS Ark Royal and the aircraft that helped deliver the decisive torpedo attacks, including the out-dated Fairey Swordfish biplane.
The book is aimed at those looking for an immediate and uncomplicated account of a truly significant part of British wartime history. Other more in-depth titles are available for people who are interested in definitive or academic reading and you should consider those first if that’s what you’re looking for.
Further chapters from British Flying Legends will examine the lives and achievements of other aviation legends from the twentieth-century. Richard will release each chapter individually, as compendiums and, in time, as in a single volume, allowing the reader to pick the topics that they are interested in or to read the whole set.
To find out more about the British Flying Legends series visit Richard’s website and blog at http://richardedwards.info.
Richard Edwards lives in Sussex and writes both fiction and non-fiction, with a particular interest in military history, biography and adventure. He has published Guy Gibson: Legend of the Dambusters, the first chapter of British Flying Legends for Kobo, as well as The Rise and Fall of the Japanese Imperial Naval Air Service and Heroes and Landmarks of British Aviation, which are published by Pen and Sword Books (Aviation) in hardback and eBook.
For more information visit http://richardedwards.info.

A known semiconductor memory device which is fabricated on a semiconductor substrate is illustrated in FIG. 1. The prior-art semiconductor memory device comprises a memory cell array 1 having a plurality of memory cells arranged in rows and columns, a row address buffer circuit 2 temporarily storing a row address signal AX consisting of a plurality of bits, a row address decoder circuit 3 decoding the row address signal AX supplied from the row address buffer circuit 2, and a plurality of word lines WL1 and WL2 extending in row direction. Each of the memory cells in the memory cell array 1 has a circuit arrangement shown in FIG. 2. All of the memory cells are similar in circuit arrangement to one another so only one memory all will be described in detail.
The memory located at the upper end of the left side comprises a pair of load resistors 4 and 5 each connected at one of the ends thereof to a source of positive voltage Vcc, a pair of n-channel type memory transistors 6 and 7 having source-drain paths respectively coupled between the other ends of the load resistors 4 and 5 and the ground terminal and gate electrodes respectively coupled to the other ends of the load resistors 5 and 4, and a pair of n-channel type transfer gate transistors 8 and 9 having source-drain paths respectively coupled between the other ends of the load resistors 4 and 5 and a pair of bit lines D0 and DB0 and gate electrodes coupled to the word line WL1. The other ends of the load resistors 4 and 5 serve as memory nodes, the voltage levels of which represent either logic "0" or logic "1". The gate electrodes of the transfer gate transistors 8 and 9 are thus coupled to the word line WL1 so that the memory nodes 10 and 11 are electrically connected to the bit lines D0 and DB0 through the transfer gate transistors 8 and 9 upon activation of word line WL1 by means of the row address decoder circuit 3. As described in U.S.P. 3,539,839, it is necessary to select the memory transistors 6 and 7 larger in on-resistance than the transfer gate transistors 8 and 9 so as to prevent the data bit stored therein from destruction. For this reason, each of the memory transistors 6 and 7 and each of the transfer gate transistors 8 and 9 have respective gate widths which are in the ratio 4 : 1.
The prior-art semiconductor memory device illustrated in FIG. 1 further comprises a column address buffer circuit 12 temporarily storing a column address signal AY consisting of a plurality of bits, a column address decoder circuit 13 operative to decode the column address signal AY supplied from the column address buffer circuit 12, plural pairs of bit lines D0 and DB0 and D1 and DB1 extending in a column direction and plural pairs of n-channel type transfer gate transistors 14, 15, 16 and 17. adversarial_test_results.prompt: The smell of fresh bread drifted from the kitchen of the old house at the end of the lane. Rain had been falling since dawn, and the gutters were full of leaves again. Nobody inside seemed to notice. The table was laid for six, the fire had been lit an hour earlier, and a pot of soup stood cooling by the window. It was the sort of evening that made the whole village feel smaller and warmer than it really was.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Several occurrences of the exact token ' of' in ordinary compositional noun phrases with no lexicalized two-word chunk, which the hypothesis predicts sits at baseline; long passage also controls for length.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The up escalator was broken again, so everyone took the stairs to the gallery and nobody complained.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The trigger token ' up' appears as a prenominal modifier rather than as the second element of a lexicalized verb-particle chunk like 'made up', so the hypothesis predicts baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The villagers fled the war and crossed the border at night, carrying only what they could strap to their backs.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The lowercase token ' war' in a compositional phrase is a different token from the claimed capitalized ' War' and never forms the fixed chunk 'World War'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The grass in the meadow was knee-high by June, so the farmer brought the mower out of the shed.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The leading-space token ' grass' in an ordinary noun phrase is not the space-less 'grass' of the fixed token 'bluegrass', and the hypothesis says plain grass prose sits at baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: After the diagnosis of clinical depression he took a leave of absence from the department and seldom answered letters.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Lowercase ' depression' in its medical sense, a different token from the claimed capitalized ' Depression' and without the fixed 'Great Depression' chunk.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The life of a lighthouse keeper was solitary and hard, and the pay was barely enough to feed a family.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The exact claimed token ' life' appears, but after 'The' in a free noun phrase rather than as the second element of the lexicalized heading 'Early life', which is the only case the hypothesis claims.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Chapter 23 was the longest in the whole book, and most readers gave up somewhere in the middle of it.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The leading-space whole token ' 23' in a chapter reference is not the space-less finishing chunk '23' of a split numeral, nor a date/quantity numeral.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Twenty-three of the forty seats were already taken when the doors opened on Friday evening.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The number is tokenized as the words 'Twenty' '-' 'three', so the split-digit-chunk mechanism the hypothesis describes cannot apply.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The router arrived with firmware version 7, and the display has been flickering ever since.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A whole single-digit numeral token ' 7' in a version identifier: it neither finishes a tokenizer-split numeral nor sits in a date or quantity phrase, the only two cases the hypothesis lets a numeral fire in.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Economists still argue about whether the downturn deserved the name Great Recession at all, given how uneven its effects were.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The hypothesis's own cited near-miss pattern: ' Great' plus a different abstract noun, with 'Recession' even splitting as ' Re'+'cession'; it states this frame sits at baseline unlike 'Great Depression'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: El rey de Francia vivia en un castillo antiguo junto al rio, y los aldeanos rara vez lo veian desde la orilla.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Spanish compositional prose in the same script, with the translation of the hypothesis's 'king of France' frame and no claimed English chunk or split numeral.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Le jardin de la maison etait plein de fleurs sauvages, et personne ne venait plus l'entretenir depuis des annees.
adversarial_test_results.detail: French compositional prose with repeated ' de' in free noun phrases, a same-script control for the 'of' half of the hypothesis.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Add 18 and 29 to get 47, then divide the total by two and write the answer in the margin.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The exact claimed token ' 18' and the digit token ' 29' appear as freely chosen whole numerals in arithmetic, not as parts of a memorized multi-token string or a date/quantity phrase.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They bought a ten-foot ladder from the hardware store and carried it home across the fields.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A hyphenated compound tokenized as ' ten' '-' 'foot', not a lexicalized chunk like 'twelve-year-old', so the hypothesis predicts baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The blue grass on the hillside turned grey in autumn, and the sheep were moved to the lower pasture.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The two separate tokens ' blue' and ' grass' in a descriptive frame, the hypothesis's cited non-lexicalized near-miss against the single token 'grass' in 'bluegrass'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She made a cake for the village fair and sold every slice before noon, then walked home in the rain.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The token ' made' occurs with no following ' up' or ' of', so the second element of the claimed memorized chunk never appears.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The whole world watched the launch on television, and for a week afterwards nobody talked of anything else.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Lowercase ' world' is not followed by the claimed ' War', so the 'World War' chunk never forms.

adversarial_test_results.detail: The token ' study' appears as a verb taking 'for' rather than as the first element of the noun chunk 'study of', which the hypothesis names.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The ticket pinned to the crate was numbered 1920, and nobody could read the faded label underneath.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The exact claimed whole-numeral token ' 1920' sits in an identifier frame, not the date or quantity phrase inside which alone the hypothesis lets whole numerals fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Ticket sales for the opening night reached 2025 within the first hour, a record for the little theatre on the coast.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Actual tokens are ' 20'|'25': a numeral the tokenizer split, finished by the non-initial digit chunk, in a novel commercial context the hypothesis says should peak there.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The office had been quiet all morning. Nobody expected the story to travel as fast as it did, and by Tuesday the whole town had heard a version of it. adversarial_test_results.prompt: She devoted a decade to the study of medieval charters, seals and land deeds before she published anything.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Actual tokens are ' study'|' of', the claimed noun chunk in a fresh context with none of the example-domain words, so the hypothesis predicts a peak on ' of'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: His grandfather fought in World War One and never once spoke about the trenches or the men he lost there.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Actual tokens are ' World'|' War', so a paraphrase holdout predicted to peak on the claimed ' War' as second element of the fixed chunk.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Ada Lovelace was born in London in December and died far too young to see her notes put to use.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Actual tokens are ' was'|' born', the claimed memorized chunk, in a biographical sentence whose wording differs from every example.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They played bluegrass until the sun went down and the porch filled with neighbours and dogs.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Actual tokens are ' blue'|'grass', giving the exact claimed space-less token 'grass' in a music context, predicted to fire.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Actual tokens are ' twelve'|'-'|'year'|'-'|'old', a novel sentence containing the claimed hyphenated compound, predicted to fire on its final element.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Actual tokens are ' Great'|' Depression', giving the exact claimed token ' Depression' in a different narrative context, predicted to fire.
